stories.headline: Abu Dhabi talks end after two days as Russia and Ukraine trade overnight strikes
stories.standfirst: The second day lasted under two hours with no immediate word on progress, while reports from the US side point to a large prisoner exchange.
body: RFE/RL reports that the US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi ended on Wednesday after a final meeting of a little under two hours, with no immediate comment on whether anything was agreed. They were the first face-to-face contact between Russian and Ukrainian officials since February. The Kyiv Independent lists Rustem Umerov, Kyrylo Budanov, Serhii Kyslytsia, David Arakhamia and Vadym Skibitsky on the Ukrainian side, with Vladimir Medinsky leading Russia and Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner for the US.

After day one Volodymyr Zelensky called the talks constructive and substantive, said humanitarian steps had been discussed and that freeing prisoners is a priority, and said security guarantees were also covered. Just Security, summarising AP, says the sides agreed a large prisoner exchange, that Kushner said numbers would be finalised the next day and that Medinsky confirmed it. No figures have been published by the sources read.

The fighting continued throughout. Ukraine's prime minister said Russia hit six major electricity facilities in four regions overnight, and Kryvyi Rih was partly left without power and heating after a drone strike. Russia's defence ministry said it destroyed 627 Ukrainian drones overnight. The Leningrad governor said 150 were shot down over his region and that a fire at the Ust-Luga port area injured three workers; two people died in Smolensk region when debris hit a flat. The Ukrainian military did not confirm attacks inside Russia.
European national security advisers, with NATO and EU officials, held separate meetings with the Ukrainian and US teams.

stories.headline: US moves tanker from RAF Mildenhall after threat as Rubio says major Iran combat no longer needed
stories.standfirst: A US refuelling aircraft left the Suffolk base after a reported Iranian threat, while Washington and Tehran continue to trade warnings.
body: The Times of Israel, citing the Wall Street Journal, reports that a US refuelling aircraft was removed from RAF Mildenhall after a threat, reportedly from Iran. It is the second such evacuation in three months: US bombers were withdrawn from RAF Fairford in September. Just Security, summarising BBC News, adds that the US Justice Department has charged three Iran-backed operatives over plots in the US and Europe, including one at an air force base in the UK. Iran denies involvement in the RAF Fairford incident.

Marco Rubio told the New York Times that economic pressure on Iran meant there was no need for major combat operations any longer, though force could return if Iran crossed certain red lines. Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei told Lebanese television that Iran would not let a single particle of enriched nuclear material leave the country and that fresh US attacks would draw strikes on US bases far away, according to Reuters as summarised by Just Security.

Iran's foreign ministry designated Argentina's navy and air force as terrorist organisations, a reciprocal move after Argentina's April designation of the Revolutionary Guards. The New York Times reportedly says Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved onto a military base over threats to his life; the severity is unclear.

stories.headline: November Windows 11 update KB5132061 fails to install for some users with 0x800F0993 and 0x800F0989
stories.standfirst: Microsoft lists no known issues for the update that carries this month's 1,000-plus fixes.
body: The Register reports that KB5132061, the November 2026 security update for Windows 11 24H2, 25H2 and 26H2, is failing to install for some users with error codes 0x800F0993 and 0x800F0989. Microsoft's support page lists no known issues for the update and the company had not commented at publication.

One user on the ElevenForum site reported that disabling Windows Sandbox, rebooting and retrying let the install complete. Others said it failed whether or not Sandbox was enabled. Other suggestions were checking the package with DISM or downloading the update manually. The update also fixes an earlier problem in which USB Audio 1.0 devices failed to start with error code 10 in Device Manager.

The month's other servicing problems add background. A September out-of-band update fixed Remote Desktop Services breakage, and October's Patch Tuesday broke Exchange Server, with a registry workaround and a fix shipped in this month's update. The Register's separate Patch Tuesday report describes more than 1,000 fixes, one of them already exploited, which Tuesday's paper covered.

sources.name: The Register, Patch Tuesday install failures

stories.headline: AMD's Mext software uses a learned page predictor to swap DRAM for NVMe flash on Epyc servers
stories.standfirst: AMD claims up to 99 per cent of performance with half the DRAM; the software is licensed and tied to its own hardware.
body: AMD acquired Mext in June 2026 and is now selling its technology as a licence for Epyc servers. A transformer-derived model predicts which memory pages will be needed next and moves them between DRAM and NVMe flash ahead of demand, so the operating system and applications still see what looks like DRAM. AMD says the model is trained on a single Epyc core in under a second, then refined over time, runs on the CPU with no GPU, and needs one core per virtual machine. How containers are handled is unclear and AMD was asked to clarify.

AMD's own figures: against Synopsys PrimeTime, offloading 50 per cent of memory to flash kept 95 per cent of DRAM-only performance, and a 25 per cent DRAM, 75 per cent flash split gave 80 per cent. For Apache Spark it claims 99 per cent with half the DRAM replaced. AMD's Gary Smerdon cites Meta research that 50 to 80 per cent of pages sit untouched for five or ten minutes, says flash is about 50 times cheaper per bit and 30 times lower power but about 500 times slower than DRAM, and claims up to 83 per cent server cost reduction. The first 145 deployed systems have reportedly avoided about $5m of DRAM spend.

Linux needs only a kernel driver. A RAM View tool helps identify suitable workloads. Phase one is OEM systems marked Mext ready, with HPE named; phase two is licences and Epyc platforms with RAM View preinstalled.

stories.headline: Baidu and Alibaba's Qwen put out ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview and Qwen4-Max Preview
stories.standfirst: Both models have a 1M-token context; only Baidu has published benchmarks, and neither lists a price per million tokens.
body: Baidu's ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview, released on 11 November, is a text-in, text-out reasoning model that is always in thinking mode. BenchLM, citing OpenRouter, lists a 1,024,000-token context. It is on Baidu's Qianfan API and a free OpenRouter route. Parameter count, maximum output and pricing are not published. BenchLM says Baidu states the post-trained weights will be released under Apache 2.0 by 25 November; the pre-trained ERNIE-5.5-Flash-Base checkpoint is already on Hugging Face under Baidu's base-model licence.

The 17 benchmark results are all Baidu's own: BrowseComp 87.4 per cent, MCP Atlas 84.6, Terminal-Bench 4.0 46.5, DeepSWE 71.2, NL2Repo 64.8, ProgramBench 29.5, Humanity's Last Exam without tools 46.4, OfficeQA Pro v2 67.9 and SpreadsheetBench 2 36.4. None is independently verified.

Qwen4-Max Preview, also dated 11 November, is a closed model with unpublished weights. The AI Release Tracker lists a 1M-token context, text, image and video input, text output, thinking mode, function calling and structured output. It is billed in credits through Alibaba Cloud's Token Plan from 10:00 on 11 November to midnight on 25 November, UTC+8, after which the preview is to be retired. No parameters, price or benchmarks are given. The vendor pages were not opened; both accounts rest on the two tracker sites.

stories.headline: Datacentre power demand has grown about 19 per cent a year against 2 per cent for US grid capacity, Howden finds
stories.standfirst: The broker's analysis says datacentres could need up to 58 per cent of their power off-grid by 2030 to hold their share steady.
body: Insurance broker Howden, using US EIA and S&P Global data, finds that power fed to US data campuses has risen about 19 per cent a year on average since 2000, while grid capacity has grown about 2 per cent a year. Datacentres took roughly 5 per cent of US grid capacity in 2025, up from 0.1 per cent in 2000.

To keep that 5 per cent share constant, Howden says datacentres might need to source up to 58 per cent of their power off-grid by 2030, which would take 110GW of behind-the-meter capacity. It regards that as unlikely and expects greater reliance on the grid, slower builds at power-constrained sites and alternative supply. Grid delays of two to six years could cost the largest constrained projects between $800m and $2.4bn in forgone revenue. Stuart Adam, Howden's head of natural resources, also says on-site generation adds operational and financial exposure.

The Register notes that Howden's chart plots grid capacity, about 1,400GW, and datacentre load, about 80GW, on different axes, so the two lines do not actually cross. It adds that Gartner said in June that AI datacentre energy use was on course to grow 26 per cent this year, and that Bain expected server-farm demand to more than double by 2030.

stories.headline: Verstappen urges Ferrari to name a number one as Mercedes celebrate their double
stories.standfirst: Norris questions Leclerc's Brazil penalty as the final three rounds of the season open with Las Vegas next week.
body: Mercedes marked their drivers' and constructors' titles at Brackley and Brixworth. Toto Wolff admitted mistakes during the team's recovery and praised the collective effort, George Russell's leadership and Kimi Antonelli's drivers' title, secured in Mexico, with the constructors' crown following in Sao Paulo. Antonelli dyed his hair in Italian colours.

Max Verstappen said Ferrari should choose a clear lead driver rather than treat Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc equally, pointing to their first-lap clash in Mexico. Ferrari team principal Frederic Vasseur has not changed policy. Lando Norris questioned the five-second penalty that dropped Leclerc from seventh to eighth after contact with Liam Lawson in Brazil, which promoted Lawson.

Grande Premio's tally over the last five rounds gives Verstappen 116 points, Antonelli 88 and Russell 26. A standings snapshot on GPBlog has Antonelli on 390, Verstappen 279, Russell 262, Hamilton 261, Leclerc 251 and Norris 246. Ferrari say they will wear black-and-yellow caps and shirts in Las Vegas. The race is on Saturday evening local time, 21 November; the sources read gave no UK session times.

stories.headline: Independent machine-learning reconstruction reproduces the ring in the 2019 M87 black hole image
stories.standfirst: A Nature paper applies a different imaging algorithm to the same Event Horizon Telescope data and gets a matching result.
body: A team of four Australian researchers led by Samuel Lai, a CSIRO postdoctoral fellow in Western Australia, published the work in Nature on 11 November. It re-processes the data behind the 2019 Event Horizon Telescope image of M87, recorded at eight telescopes including sites in Chile, the US and Antarctica.

Their method is an independent, machine-learning imaging algorithm that works from closed triplets, closure quantities across three telescopes, rather than pairs of stations, which reduces certain errors. The Register reports that it recreates the ring structure and matches the original in size and shape. Lai says the model had no prior knowledge of what a black hole looks like.
EHT director Laurent Loinard welcomed the paper as independent confirmation of the ring structure across several years of data.

today: Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend runs 19 to 21 November, with the race on Saturday evening local time.
Qwen4-Max Preview access ends at midnight UTC+8 on 25 November; Baidu says ERNIE 5.5 Flash weights are due under Apache 2.0 by the same date.

briefs.text: Nvidia has hired former acting SDNY US attorney Joon H. Kim to investigate Jensen Huang, according to Axios, the New York Times and Reuters as summarised by Just Security.

NATO jets were scrambled after at least four drones strayed into Baltic airspace during Ukrainian strikes on Russia, and Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia issued shelter alerts; no injuries were reported.
A US federal judge rejected the BBC's bid to dismiss Donald Trump's defamation suit over edits to his 6 January speech, per Politico as summarised by Just Security.
The UK Privy Council struck down Trinidad and Tobago's colonial-era ban on gay sex, according to AP as summarised by Just Security.

A Heathrow Terminal 2 information screen was spotted showing a Linux boot log, including systemd, an Intel PRO/1000 adapter and an ext4 volume named LV_ROOT, as the airport rolls out Raspberry Pi signage.
